# 2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game
The 2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game was a National Football League (NFL) regular season game played on December 15, 2013, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. In this Week 15 matchup, the Green Bay Packers overcame a 23-point halftime deficit to defeat the Dallas Cowboys by a score of 37–36, tying the largest comeback victory in Packers franchise history. Green Bay’s backup quarterback Matt Flynn threw four touchdown passes in the second half, including the go-ahead score, while Dallas quarterback Tony Romo threw two interceptions in the final minutes that enabled the Packers’ rally. With the victory, Green Bay improved to 7–6–1 and kept its playoff hopes alive, and the loss dropped Dallas to 7–7, hurting the Cowboys’ chances in the NFC East race.
## Background
The game took place in Week 15 of the 2013 NFL season and had significant playoff implications for both teams. The Green Bay Packers entered with a 6–6–1 record and were still in contention for the NFC North title despite having lost star quarterback Aaron Rodgers to a broken collarbone in early November. Rodgers had missed six straight games and was not yet medically cleared to return, so Green Bay continued to start Matt Flynn at quarterback. The Dallas Cowboys, at 7–6, were fighting for the NFC East crown and sought to pull even with the Philadelphia Eagles atop the division. The Cowboys were playing at home in Arlington, where the Packers had not won a game since 1989. The matchup was also notable as Green Bay’s first visit to AT&T Stadium since winning Super Bowl XLV on that field in the 2010 season.
## Game summary
First half: The Cowboys dominated the first half, building a 26–3 lead by halftime. Dallas opened the scoring with two field goals by Dan Bailey (47 and 23 yards) and a 25-yard touchdown pass from Tony Romo to Jason Witten in the first quarter. In the second quarter Bailey added two more field goals (43 and 50 yards), and running back DeMarco Murray capped the half with a 1-yard touchdown run in the final minute before intermission. Bailey made five field goals in total during the game, accounting for much of Dallas’s early scoring. Meanwhile, Green Bay’s only first-half points came on a franchise-record-tying 57-yard field goal by Mason Crosby in the first quarter. By halftime, Dallas led 26–3 and appeared in full control, having outgained Green Bay and forced two Packers turnovers.
Second half: The momentum swung dramatically after halftime. On the very first play of the third quarter, Packers running back Eddie Lacy broke free for a 60-yard run, energizing the team. That drive led to Green Bay’s first touchdown just minutes into the half, as Matt Flynn found Jordy Nelson for a 13-yard scoring pass to cut the deficit to 26–10. Dallas answered with Bailey’s fifth field goal (another 50-yarder) to make it 29–10. However, Green Bay continued to chip away: Flynn threw a 3-yard touchdown to Andrew Quarless late in the third quarter, and early in the fourth he connected with James Starks on an 11-yard touchdown. Those scores suddenly brought the Packers within five points, at 29–24, with about 13 minutes remaining in the game.
Facing Green Bay’s surge, the Cowboys briefly regained momentum with a 5-yard touchdown pass from Romo to Dez Bryant, extending the Dallas lead to 36–24 with 7:55 left in the fourth quarter. Bryant’s leaping catch in the end zone over multiple defenders appeared to put Dallas back in control. But the Packers offense responded immediately: Flynn led another drive and threw his fourth touchdown of the half, a 3-yard strike to James Jones, making the score 36–31 with just over four minutes remaining. It was Green Bay’s fifth consecutive touchdown drive in the second half, completing an improbable comeback from the 23-point deficit.
In the final minutes, the game saw a dramatic finish. Clinging to a five-point lead (36–31) with under three minutes left, the Cowboys had a chance to run out the clock. Dez Bryant had gained a first down just before the two-minute warning, and Dallas was in position to force Green Bay to use its timeouts. However, on a 2nd-and-6 play with about 1:50 remaining, Tony Romo audibled to a pass play (instead of a handoff to Murray) and threw the ball behind receiver Miles Austin while trying to escape pressure. The pass was intercepted by Green Bay cornerback Sam Shields at midfield, giving the Packers another opportunity with very little time left. Green Bay quickly drove 50 yards, and Eddie Lacy scored on a 1-yard touchdown plunge with 1:31 remaining – the Packers’ first lead of the game, coming after they had trailed 26–3 at halftime. The Packers attempted a two-point conversion to increase the lead to a field goal margin, but Flynn’s pass to Quarless was no good, leaving the score 37–36.
Dallas still had a chance to respond, needing only a field goal in the final 90 seconds. However, on the Cowboys’ very next possession, Romo threw another interception. He attempted a pass toward Cole Beasley that was initially ruled incomplete, but Green Bay’s Tramon Williams had dived under the throw to snag it just above the turf. After a video review, the call was reversed to an interception by Williams, effectively sealing the outcome. The Packers ran out the remaining time with kneeldowns. Notably, an upset Dez Bryant left the field and headed to the locker room before the game had officially ended, drawing some criticism for his early exit.
## Aftermath and significance
Green Bay’s comeback from a 23-point deficit is tied for the largest in the Packers’ long history, matching a 1982 game in which the team also overcame a 23-point gap (against the Los Angeles Rams). The 37–36 victory was the Packers’ first road win in Dallas since 1989, ending a multi-decade drought in away games against the Cowboys. The game was widely regarded as one of the most exciting of the 2013 NFL season; the NFL named the Packers’ rally a nominee for the league’s “Never Say Never Moment” of Week 15, recognizing its improbability and dramatic finish. Packers head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters after the game that the emotional comeback victory left him “drained” and was as exhilarating as any in his career. On the Dallas side, owner Jerry Jones called it “one of the hardest losses” he had ever experienced, and the Cowboys’ collapse in the second half intensified criticism of their play-calling and late-game execution. Some observers questioned the decision to pass instead of run in the critical moment before Romo’s first interception, given DeMarco Murray’s success on the ground (134 rushing yards in the game at a 7.4-yard average).
The win kept the Packers in contention for the postseason. Green Bay improved to 7–6–1 and remained just a half-game behind the NFC North leaders. In fact, injured quarterback Aaron Rodgers returned to action in Week 17, and the Packers would go on to win their final two games and clinch the NFC North title at 8–7–1. For Dallas, the defeat proved costly. The Cowboys fell to 7–7 and remained one game behind Philadelphia in the NFC East with two weeks remaining. Although Dallas still controlled its own destiny at that point (with two divisional games left), they ultimately finished 8–8 for the third straight year and missed the playoffs once again. The 2013 loss to Green Bay, marked by surrendering a 23-point lead at home, has since been remembered as a defining moment of the Cowboys’ late-season struggles in that era, and a highlight in NFL lore for the Packers’ resilience.

Published: Dec 18, 2013 at 04:20 AM

It was [a shocking setback](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299650/article/dallas-cowboys-continue-to-feature-a-flair-for-the-catastrophic) for America's so-called team, and [the ripple effect of this game](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299684/article/jason-garretts-job-at-risk-if-cowboys-miss-playoffs) might be felt for weeks to come. The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) stormed out to a 26-3 halftime lead against what appeared for 30 minutes of play to be a totally overmatched [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) team that was without starting quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://www.nfl.com/player/aaronrodgers/2506363/profile) for the sixth consecutive game. Instead, Green Bay emerged from the locker room following halftime a rejuvenated bunch and rallied in the second half for the biggest comeback in franchise history in [a 37-36 win](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013121512/2013/REG15/packers@cowboys#tab=recap&menu=highlights&recap=fullstory) in the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL)' own ballpark. It was one of the most exciting finishes of the season, and the events that led up to the victorious moment for Green Bay will be discussed and debated for a long time.

Here are the key moments before the moment:

### Cowboys build massive halftime lead

### Lacy sets tone for second half

**The play:**[Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) rookie running back [Eddie Lacy](https://www.nfl.com/player/eddielacy/2540168/profile) breaks free for a 60-yard gain on the first play from scrimmage in the second half.

**The aftermath:** A [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) team that was dormant in the first half suddenly sprang to life in an instant, with Lacy setting the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) up nicely for their first touchdown of the game. That score came three plays later, as quarterback [Matt Flynn](https://www.nfl.com/player/mattflynn/367/profile) hit receiver [Jordy Nelson](https://www.nfl.com/player/jordynelson/1032/profile) for [a 13-yard touchdown play](http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-cant-miss-plays/0ap2000000298577/WK-15-Can-t-Miss-Play-Nelson-snatches-it-from-Cowboy) that trimmed Dallas' lead to 26-10. It was an amazing play by Nelson, who snatched what could have been an interception away from [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) defensive back [Orlando Scandrick](https://www.nfl.com/player/orlandoscandrick/2307/profile) for the score.

### Packers' comeback is nearly complete

**The play:** Running back [James Starks](https://www.nfl.com/player/jamesstarks/497206/profile) catches a short pass from Flynn and goes 11 yards for a touchdown.

**The aftermath:** Starks' touchdown, coupled with tight end [Andrew Quarless' score](http://www.nfl.com/videos/green-bay-packers/0ap2000000298601/Quarless-3-yard-TD-reception) on the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB)' previous possession, cut the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL)' lead down to five at 29-24. With nearly 13 minutes still left to play, there was plenty of time for the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to complete the improbable comeback.

### Cowboys strike back

**The play:** Quarterback [Tony Romo](https://www.nfl.com/player/tonyromo/2505354/profile) finds receiver [Dez Bryant](https://www.nfl.com/player/dezbryant/497278/profile) in the back of the end zone for a 5-yard touchdown play.

**The aftermath:** It was an amazing scoring snag by Bryant, who somehow managed to catch the ball among a host of [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) defenders and get two feet down before momentum carried him out of bounds. With less than eight minutes left, the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) were up 36-24 and perhaps had weathered the frantic second-half rally of the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB).

### Romo throws first of two costly interceptions

### Lacy puts the Pack on top

**The play:** With massive defensive linemen [Mike Daniels](https://www.nfl.com/player/mikedaniels/2532826/profile) and [B.J. Raji](https://www.nfl.com/player/b.j.raji/79631/profile) lined up at fullback, Lacy burst through for a 1-yard touchdown dive for the go-ahead score.

**The aftermath:** Lacy put an exclamation point on the score with an emphatic spike of the football. The comeback was complete and the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) led 37-36. A two-point conversion try failed, so all the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) needed was a field goal to win. There was plenty of time for Romo and the Dallas offense to pull if off, too, as there was a minute and a half left on the game clock.

### The moment

**The play:**[Romo throws the second](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000298801/article/tony-romos-interceptions-cap-wild-packers-comeback) of two costly interceptions. This one to [Tramon Williams](https://www.nfl.com/player/tramonwilliams/2506789/profile) on a play that was initially ruled incomplete but then reversed following an instant-replay review.

**The aftermath:** A most implausible rally by the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) in a frenzied second half was complete. As Green Bay maintained hope in its quest to reach the playoffs, Dallas missed out on a grand opportunity to take sole possession of first place in the NFC East. While the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL)[were left with goats in the epic collapse](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299442/article/tony-romo-gets-heat-what-about-monte-kiffin-jason-garrett), the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB)' Flynn [achieved hero status](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299492/article/green-bay-packers-quarterback-matt-flynn-hero) in what has been a roller-coaster 2013 for the quarterback.

Orton INT seals Eagles' win over Cowboys
========================================

Published: Dec 29, 2013 at 04:11 PM

*   
*   
*   
*   Copied!

ARLINGTON, Texas -- [Nick Foles](https://www.nfl.com/player/nickfoles/2532842/profile) threw two touchdown passes, NFL rushing champion [LeSean McCoy](https://www.nfl.com/player/leseanmccoy/79607/profile) had 120 yards and a receiving score and the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://www.nfl.com/teams/philadelphiaeagles/profile?team=PHI) beat the [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) 24-22 in a win-or-go-home game for the NFC East title Sunday night.

**On NFL Network**  
_NFL Replay_  
will re-air the [Philadelphia Eagles' 24-22 victory](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013122903/2013/REG17/eagles@cowboys) over the [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) from Week 17 on Tuesday, Dec. 30 at 3 p.m. ET.

» **[NFL Network schedule](http://www.nfl.com/nflnetwork/networkschedule)**

The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) (8-8), with [Kyle Orton](https://www.nfl.com/player/kyleorton/2506444/profile) filling in two days after [Tony Romo](https://www.nfl.com/player/tonyromo/2505354/profile) had back surgery, lost to a division rival with a playoff berth on the line for the third straight year.

The [Eagles](https://www.nfl.com/teams/philadelphiaeagles/profile?team=PHI) (10-6) will host New Orleans a wild-card game Saturday night.

Dallas trailed 24-16 when Orton threw a 32-yard touchdown pass to [Dez Bryant](https://www.nfl.com/player/dezbryant/497278/profile). Orton went back to Bryant for the 2-point conversion, but the ball fell incomplete.

The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) got another chance with a stop from their beleaguered defense, but Orton's pass was intercepted by [Brandon Boykin](https://www.nfl.com/player/brandonboykin/2532798/profile) on the first play to seal the win.

McCoy finished with 1,596 yards.

ARLINGTON, Texas — If this was Matt Flynn’s last start in place of Aaron Rodgers, it was quite a memorable one.

Flynn threw four touchdown passes in the second half, Eddie Lacy had the winning score on a 1-yard plunge after an interception by Tony Romo gave them one more chance, and the Green Bay Packers matched the biggest comeback in franchise history in a 37-36 win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.

Romo tossed two interceptions in the final 3 minutes, the first one giving Green Bay a chance for the go-ahead score with the Cowboys in position to run out the clock with a 36-31 lead.

Lacy scored with 1:31 to go for Green Bay’s first lead since the first quarter and after the Packers trailed 26-3 at halftime.

"It took me everything not to cry," said Packers coach Mike McCarthy, whose team won its second straight without Rodgers after going winless in the first five, including the Chicago game when the star QB got hurt. "I’m just drained. Just the sheer emotion. It was incredible."

Playing on the same field where Rodgers was the MVP when they won the 2011 Super Bowl, the Packers matched the 1982 team in a September game against the Los Angeles Rams for the largest rally.

The Packers (7-6-1) kept their playoff hopes alive with Rodgers possibly returning next week. He was close to medical clearance, but missed his sixth straight game with a broken collarbone. He was wearing on a headset on Green Bay’s sideline.

"Most guys would pack it in — ‘Guys, it’s not our season. Let’s go home and get ready for next year,"’ said Green Bay cornerback Tramon Williams, who had an interception overturned on review before a game-clinching pick that was ruled incomplete and reversed on replay. "It’s not that vibe here."

The vibe in Dallas could negative for a while, with Dez Bryant walking off the field before the game ended and refusing to talk to reporters in the locker room, simply shaking his head at them after finishing with 153 yards and a touchdown.

"This is one of the hardest losses that I’ve experienced," Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said. "That’s a shame that we’ve lost that ballgame."

The Cowboys (7-7) blew a great chance to pull even with Philadelphia in the NFC East but still control their playoff fate. They finish with Washington and the Eagles.

"We still control what we feel like we can get done," Romo said. "It just doesn’t feel like it right now because we let it slip away."

With Dallas leading 36-31, Bryant made a lunging first down after a catch just before the 2-minute warning that looked as if it would Dallas help hold off a huge Green Bay rally. But Romo threw behind Miles Austin after escaping a sack and Sam Shields intercepted at midfield.

The Packers steadily moved downfield before the plunge by Lacy, who had 141 yards rushing.

Behind for the first time since the first quarter, Romo threw a ball too far in front of Cole Beasley, and Williams made a diving grab that was initially called incomplete. When the video review overturned the call, Flynn ended the game with kneel-downs.

"Right now, words really have no effect," Dallas cornerback Brandon Carr said. "Complete debacle the second half. We’ve just got to get better, man."

Williams had an earlier interception overturned on review with Dallas clinging to a 29-24 lead. He cradled a deflected pass in his arms and had a weaving return to inside the Dallas 10, but replayed showed the nose of ball hitting the turf.

The Cowboys went on to score when Bryant made a leaping grab over M.D. Jennings and got two feet down in the back of the end zone for a 36-24 lead.

Flynn answered with his fourth straight scoring drive to get the Packers back within five. A Dallas defence that gave up eight straight scoring drives to Chicago in a loss last week let the Packers get touchdowns on five straight drives after halftime.

"What a feelin’!"’ said Flynn, who threw for 299 yards with one interception. "As we were taking a knee, we were thinking ‘Is this real? Is this happening?"’

Romo threw for 358 yards and two touchdowns, but couldn’t avoid two more critical mistakes in a career at least partially defined by them.

**NOTES:** DeMarco Murray had 134 yards rushing and a touchdown for Dallas. … Dan Bailey had five field goals for Dallas. Mason Crosby hit a 57-yarder for the Packers. … Packers DE Johnny Jolly left the game with a shoulder injury. TE Brandon Bostick came out with a foot injury. … The Cowboys ended up without their top four linebackers after Justin Durant (hamstring) and Ernie Sims (hip) were knocked out. They were already playing without Sean Lee and Bruce Carter.

Cowboys Surrender 23-Point Lead, Fall 37-36 To Packers
======================================================

December 15, 2013 / 7:02 PM CST / CBS Texas

[Add CBS News on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbsnews.com)

**ARLINGTON (CBSDFW/AP) —** Matt Flynn and the Green Bay Packers matched the biggest comeback in franchise history. Tony Romo and the Dallas Cowboys have a loss that might sting for a long time.

Flynn threw four touchdown passes in the second half, Eddie Lacy had the winning score on a 1-yard plunge after an interception by Romo gave them another chance, and the Packers rallied from 23 points down at halftime to beat the Cowboys 37-36 Sunday.

[_**\>>PHOTOS: Packers 37, Cowboys 36<<**_](http://cbsloc.al/1bJ7BIL)

Romo tossed two interceptions in the final 3 minutes, the first one giving Green Bay a chance for the go-ahead score with the Cowboys in position to run out the clock with a 36-31 lead. Lacy scored with just over 1 1-2 minutes left.

"This obviously falls in the tough loss category" Romo said after the game. "We let one slip away and we didn't execute across the board."

### Cowboys QB Tony Romo p0st game press conference

 Your browser does not support the audio element.

"Probably one of the toughest losses in my short NFL career," said safety Barry Church after the game. "Things started to unravel. They got momentum and we weren't able to seize it back."

Playing on the same field where they won the 2011 Super Bowl, the Packers matched the 1982 team, which rallied past the Los Angeles Rams after trailing by 23.

The Packers (7-6-1) kept their playoff hopes alive with Aaron Rodgers possibly returning next week.

The Cowboys (7-7) blew a great chance to pull even with Philadelphia in the NFC East, remaining a game behind with two to play.

Dez Bryant, who had 153 yards receiving, had picked up a first down just before the 2-minute warning that looked as if it would Dallas help hold off a huge Green Bay rally. But Romo threw behind Miles Austin after escaping a sack and Sam Shields intercepted at midfield.

The Packers steadily moved downfield before the plunge by Lacy, who had 141 yards rushing.

Behind for the first time since the first quarter, Romo threw a ball too far in front of Cole Beasley, and Tramon Williams made a diving grab that was initially called incomplete. When the video review overturned the call, Flynn ended the game with kneel-downs.

Bryant walked off the field and into the tunnel before the game ended.

Williams had an earlier interception overturned on review with Dallas clinging to a 29-24 lead. He cradled a deflected pass in his arms, but officials reviewed that the nose of ball hit the turf.

The Cowboys went on to score when Bryant made a leaping grab over M.D. Jennings and got two feet down in the back of the end zone for a 36-24 lead.

Flynn answered with his fourth straight scoring drive to get back within five. He finished with 299 yards passing, including second-half scoring tosses of 13 yards to Jordy Nelson, 3 yards to Andrew Quarless, 11 yards to James Starks and 3 yards to James Jones.

Romo threw for 358 yards to break a four-game streak where he didn't have more than 250, but the late interceptions will only fuel the feeling his critical mistakes will keep the Cowboys from going deep in playoffs for the first time since their last Super Bowl title during the 1995 season.

Rodgers was the MVP when the Packers beat Pittsburgh for the Super Bowl title on Dallas' home field, but this time he had to watch from the sideline with a headset after doctors didn't clear him to play, forcing to miss his sixth straight game since breaking his left collarbone.

DeMarco Murray had 134 yards rushing and a touchdown for Dallas.

Dallas still controls its own destiny in the NFC East, traveling to Washington next Sunday before hosting Philadelphia in the finale.

"We've just got to stick together and fight through all this adversity," said Brandon Carr. "Wins cure all in this league. We all know that."

Despite the loss, veteran defender DeMarcus Ware said he is not ready to give up. "We don't give up here. Good players come back from adversity and this is an adverse time, and we still have a chance."

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was not as forgiving saying "this one is the hardest losses that i've experienced. That's a shame that we lost that ballgame."
